newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo sells Renault stake for 5.9 bln SKR.
newsitem.headline: Volvo sells Renault stake for 5.9 bln SKR.

text.p: Swedish vehicle maker AB Volvo said on Thursday it had sold its entire stake in French car maker Renault to Union Bank of Switzerland for 5.9 billion crowns ($743.3 million) to sell it to international investors.
Volvo said the sale, which was in line with a continuing divestment programme to focus on core businesses, will give a capital gain of 750 million crowns.
The stake amounted to 11.38 percent of Renault, or about 27.2 million shares, the company said in a statement.
"The sale of our stake in Renault is fully in line with the strategy the board decided on at the start of 1994," Volvo Chief Executive Leif Johansson said in the statement.
"We are selling now to realise the upturn in the Renault share in 1997, which has been further accentuated over the past week."
Two days ago Volvo denied market rumours it had sold its Renault stake.
Volvo has previously said it also intends to sell its four percent stake of Swedish/U.S. drugs group Pharmacia & Upjohn.
"It's not on the cards right now (to sell P&U shares)," Volvo spokesman Stefan Karlsson told Reuters.
Volvo was trading 1.5 crowns higher at 213.5 crowns at 1200 GMT with the Stockholm general index weaker across the board, falling 0.25 percent.
